claims.text: The rider's core artifacts describe one and the same trip, which is the first limb of her burden under POL-RD-08. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00519; the trace runs from the recorded trip start at 2026-09-07T08:06:40+08:00 to its end at 08:18:40+08:00, and every fix is at the 10 second cadence with 100% coverage and no gaps. The fare ledger is charged against the same trip. I put this no higher than it goes: it establishes identity of the trip, not a deviation.

The in-app chat log corroborates the rider's account that she gave a specific routing instruction and got no answer. She sent 'take Clementi Rd then North Buona Vista, fewer lights' at 08:08:10; the driver read it at 08:08:35 and did not reply; her follow-up 'hello?' at 08:10:40 likewise drew no reply. The instruction names two specific roads, which is the very level of specificity POL-RD-04 treats as an instruction a driver can act on ('take the AYE, not the PIE'), so the rider's request was neither vague nor unheard. The driver's own statement in the counterparty_statement - 'She wanted a different road; I'm not obliged to take passenger shortcuts' - confirms the request was received and declined. That is the substance of the rider's complaint, and on this evidence it is one-sided rather than imagined.

I have to be straight about the threshold, because stretching it would cost the claim rather than win it. On the governing figure - gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 2.71 km against a 5.0 km optimal route - the excess is MINUS 2.29 km, or -45.8%, because the rider alighted early at 'Commonwealth Ave W, rider alighted early'. Neither POL-RD-01 establishment test (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute) can pass on a negative excess, so no route deviation is established on this trip's own trace and no POL-RD-02 recomputation is available to the rider. Running that arithmetic anyway on this record, the recomputed optimal fare of 10.87 exceeds the 9.99 actually charged, so a POL-RD-02 refund floors at zero and the de minimis rule would give NO_ACTION regardless. The rider's distance-and-time grievance cannot be sustained, and I do not pretend otherwise.

The one proviso in POL-RD-01 that survives a failed threshold is a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09, and I have checked it and must report that it too is empty. The fare breakdown itemises no ERP gantries at all (erp_gantries is an empty list, tolls_erp 0.00), carries no airport surcharge (0.00) on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and every charge line has a counterpart in the trace or the trip record - base fare 3.80; distance 2.03 for the 2.7 km actually driven; time 3.36 for the 12 minutes actually driven; platform fee 0.80. I do not assert a phantom or unmatched charge, because there is none. On this record the contested 9.99 is correctly computed, and naming that honestly is more useful to the tribunal than an unsupported billing-integrity point.

claims.text: The governing measurement shows the driver drove LESS far than the platform's optimal route, not more. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 2.71 km against an optimal_distance_km of 5.0 km, an excess of minus 2.29 km, i.e. -45.8%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds 20% of optimal_distance_km AND exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms. A negative excess passes neither limb, so no route deviation exists on this trip and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the journey.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. Here the two do not straddle anything: 2.71 km (trace) against 2.70 km (trip record convenience copy). Both readings are far below the 5.0 km optimal, so there is no excess to measure on either figure.

The reason the measured distance falls short of the optimal route is the rider's own decision to get out of the vehicle. The trip_record dropoff is expressly labelled 'Commonwealth Ave W, rider alighted early', and the trip is recorded as COMPLETED at 2.7 km against a 5.0 km optimal. A journey the rider cuts short cannot be converted into a driver route deviation under POL-RD-01.

POL-RD-02's fare recomputation runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'. No deviation is established on this trace, so the rider has no distance-or-time remedy at all and the NO_ACTION consequence of POL-RD-01 governs.

Even if POL-RD-02 were run, it refunds charged_total less a recomputed fare, and the arithmetic yields nothing. The recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 5.0 + 0.28 x 9.0) x surge_multiplier 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee = (3.80 + 3.75 + 2.52 + 0.80) = 10.87, against a charged_total of 9.99. The refund floors at zero (the fare ledger shows a quantum of 0.05, below the 0.50 de minimis), so no money is owed on the distance and time lines in any event. The rider was in fact charged less than the optimal-route metered fare.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show (a) that the artifacts describe the same trip and (b) an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. The trace is clean for both schema and policy purposes (coverage_pct 100.0, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0, weight 1.0), and it shows a negative excess. The burden is therefore not discharged and never shifts to the driver.

No standalone pass-through or billing-integrity refund is due under POL-RD-09(4). The fare_breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines at all (erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp 0.0, optimal_route_erp 0.0) and no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.0). There is no phantom line to correct, so limb (4) is not engaged and no billing-integrity referral arises.

The rider's chat instruction does not create a deviation or an entitlement. The message 'take Clementi Rd then North Buona Vista, fewer lights' names roads but carries waypoint_hint null, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test cannot even be run; and POL-RD-04 governs only a deviation caused by a rider request, which is the converse of this trip, where the driver stayed on the app corridor and drove the shortest measured path of the day. Her separate complaint that the driver 'did not even reply' is not a route deviation and grounds no monetary remedy in this category.

The disputed payment stands unreversed: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative, and on this rider-filed dispute it leaves that charge exactly as it is. Since the excess claim fails at POL-RD-01, leaving the present state standing is the correct outcome.

The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00519-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and can carry no fact for either side. The driver does not invoke POL-RD-03 and asserts no external traffic cause, so no advisory is needed to explain this trip; the absence of one is a gap in the bundle and not a defect in the driver's route, which was simply shorter than optimal.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The claim fails on the measurement, and it fails in the rider's own favour to state it plainly.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip record. The trace reads 2.71 km; the platform's optimal route for this booking is 5.0 km. The excess is therefore minus 2.29 km, i.e. -45.8%. A deviation is established only where the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms; a negative excess passes neither test. No route deviation exists on this trip, and the consequence POL-RD-01 sets for that is NO_ACTION however the journey is characterised. The shortfall is explained by the rider's own decision: the trip record's dropoff is labelled 'Commonwealth Ave W, rider alighted early' and the trip is logged COMPLETED at 2.7 km against a 5.0 km optimal. A journey cut short by the rider cannot be turned into a driver deviation.

POL-RD-02 consequently does not run, because it applies only where a deviation is established. Even run for completeness it gives nothing: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 5.0 + 0.28 x 9.0) x surge 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee = 10.87 recomputed, against 9.99 actually charged. The refund floors at zero, and the fare ledger's quantum of 0.05 is below the 0.50 de minimis in any event. The rider was in fact charged less than the metered optimal-route fare.

On the rider's communication grievance: the chat log shows she sent 'take Clementi Rd then North Buona Vista, fewer lights' at 08:08:10, the driver read it at 08:08:35 without replying, and her follow-up 'hello?' at 08:10:40 also went unanswered. That is on the record and I do not minimise it. But POL-RD-04 governs exonerating a deviation caused by a rider instruction - the converse of this trip, where the driver drove a shorter path than optimal - and its corroboration test cannot even be run here because the message carries waypoint_hint null. Its separate compensation limb requires the rider to have been billed more than 1.0 km less than the trace records; the fare ledger bills 2.7 km against a 2.71 km trace, a 0.01 km difference, so no driver compensation arises either. No clause in the ROUTE_DEVIATION category provides a monetary remedy for a driver declining a routing request, and the driver's own statement ('I follow the app route, that's the rule') confirms the request was received and declined rather than disputed.

On billing integrity under POL-RD-09: the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00) and no airport surcharge (0.00) on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. Every charge line has a counterpart in the trace or the trip record. There is no phantom or unmatched line, so limb (4) is not engaged and no billing-integrity referral arises.

The driver's repeat-deviation check under POL-RD-06 does not fire: deviation_flags_90d is 0, so no trailing pattern is established and no driver-conduct referral follows, there being no MATERIAL deviation to begin with.

The bundle's traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00519-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and can carry no fact; no party invoked a traffic cause, so its absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a defect in the driver's route. The DRIVER claim resting on it was discarded for non-disclosure of its issue code and is not relied on here.

Confidence: the deciding facts - the trace distance and the optimal distance - are carried by the GPS trace and the trip record, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap under POL-GEN-02(2) is 1.0 and the 0.70 escalation floor is comfortably cleared. The contested 9.99 stands and is not refunded; fare_breakdown.payment_status remains CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

To both parties: the measurements decide this one, and both advocates agree on them.

ROUTE. The governing distance figure is the GPS trace, 2.71 km (POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing field and forbids citing the trip record's rounded copy for the threshold test).
